ms.report:
Preamble: Quick apologize for having misunderstood the POA submission process in this milestone. We were under the impression we were to submit what we had ready by the December POA deadline, but as we wrote ourselves we were not yet satisfied with the results at that point, and we are happy to resubmit now in January at a point where the Code of Conduct is at a state ready for the workshops after several rounds of feedback. 
Output: 
Evolve dRep documents from v0.1 to v1.0:
We have evolved the DRep document to one single DRep Code of Conduct document instead of a separate code of conduct for the catalyst and CIP 1694 DReps and have worked extensively to simplify from an at most 24 pages document to a now 9-pager with a graphical version further simplifying it for the first workshop in Norway 20th January as a supplement. We believe this is a good approach when we use the Code of Conduct for discussions in the workshops to further it and make it easier to understand for an audience that can range from people with deep knowledge of Cardano Governance to people without much knowledge of Cardano governance. Less is more is a saying we think applies to this document and we hope the reviewers understand this means a lot of work has gone into simplifying the code of conduct and this is well within the milestone output of evolving it from 0.1 to v1.0. (We believe there is no requirement of a large length or a lot of new novel items unless the community actually wanted other items in their feedback). See also the version history of the document for an objective data point of all the comments and edits that have been done with around 50 versions from December 12th to January 14th. 
Each week, open dRep documents to the Catalyst community for comments and discussion. Repeat iterations until the community feels all needs are addressed or until the third week of December:
When it comes to the weekly feedback until the third week of December we did not feel we had sufficient fee

ms.report:
For milestone 3 we were to hold in-person events in 5 locations across the world: Norway, Ghana, Japan, USA, and Colombia. The acceptance criteria were a written summary in English of the event as well as collected data on the agenda items from the workshop. 
The evidence of this completion would be a forum post on the Cardano Foundations forum with a summary of each workshop and that the collected data is publicly available on the Cardano Foundations Forums.
Note that how the data was presented in the forum post has been individual with some posting the Miro board pictures and others a more written paragraph summary but we also will aggregate the feedback we got as part of the next milestone. 
 On the 20th of January, the first workshop was held in Oslo Norway and the forum post with the data collected can be found here: https://forum.cardano.org/t/drep-code-of-conduct-workshop-in-oslo/127035
On the 27th of January, the second workshop was held in Accra, Ghana and the forum post with the data collected can be funded here: https://forum.cardano.org/t/drep-code-of-conduct-workshop-accra-ghana/127464
Then on the 17th of February, a workshop was held in Indianapolis, USA and the forum post with the data collected can be found here:https://forum.cardano.org/t/drep-code-of-conduct-workshop-indianapolis/128335
Shortly after on the 21st of February, a workshop was held in Tokyo, Japan and the forum post with the data collected can be found here: https://forum.cardano.org/t/drep-february-2024-tokyo-workshop-and-meetup/128063
Finally, on the 24th of February, a workshop was held in Bogota, Colombia and the forum post with the data collected can be found here: https://forum.cardano.org/t/drep-recruitment-training-and-ethical-code-of-conduct-workshop-bogota-colombia/128363
